newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securitas positive on outlook for '97.
newsitem.headline: Securitas positive on outlook for '97.

text.p: Swedish security company Securitas said on Friday that it expected to see continued good sales and profit growth in 1997.
For 1996 Securitas posted a 17 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 550 million crowns with sales increasing 24 percent to 9.07 billion crowns.
"The phase of organic growth which began during 1996 continued at a rate of seven percent during 1996," president and chief executive Thomas Berglund said in a statement.
"Acquisitions raised sales by 1.78 billion crowns during 1996.
"The organic growth and the acquisitions completed will contribute to a continued good development of sales and income (in 1997)."
Acquisitions in 1996 were made in Germany, Britain, France, Portugal, Sweden, Finland, Poland and Estonia. All were paid for in cash.
"Sales will increase by about 2.7 billion crowns on an annual basis," Berglund said.
Securitas said all 13 countries where it operates, bar Austria, are showing growth. Operations in Hungary, Denmark and Switzerland have shown robust volume growths.
Its major market remains Sweden accounting for 28 percent of total sales followed by Germany with 18 percent, Spain with 14 percent and Norway with 11 percent.
Securitas's board proposed a dividend for 1996 of 2.40 crowns compared to 2.00 crowns a year earlier.
